transcript.text: roomba e5 wont charge properly, sometimes it does sometimes it doesnt

Intermittent charging on an e5 is usually caused by dirty contacts, a poor connection with the dock, or an aging battery. Here's what to try, roughly from easiest to hardest:

## 1. Clean the charging contacts (most common fix)
• On the robot: Flip it over and find the two metal charging contacts near the front. Wipe them with a cloth dampened with rubbing alcohol (or a melamine sponge/Magic Eraser for buildup).
• On the Home Base: Clean the two metal contacts on the dock the same way.
• Do this every few weeks. Dust and carpet residue build up fast and cause exactly this on/off behavior.

## 2. Check the dock's spring contacts
• Press the dock contacts down with your finger. They should spring back up freely. If one sticks or feels weak, the robot may only connect sometimes.

## 3. Check dock placement and power
• Place the dock on a hard, level surface against a wall, not on thick carpet.
• Leave about 1.5 ft (0.5 m) of clearance on each side and 4 ft (1.2 m) in front.
• Make sure the power cord is firmly plugged into both the dock and the outlet. Try a different outlet (avoid ones controlled by a light switch).
• Look for a small light on the dock that confirms it's getting power.

## 4. Test whether it's a docking or charging problem
• Place the robot on the dock by hand and watch the light:
• Pulsing amber = charging
• Solid white/green = fully charged
• No light / red = not charging
• If it charges fine when placed by hand but not on its own, it's a docking/navigation issue. Clean the sensors on the front and underside, and make sure nothing blocks the dock.

## 5. Reset the robot
• Press and hold the CLEAN button for about 20 seconds until the light ring swirls white, then release. This reboots the software.
• Also check the iRobot Home app for firmware updates and any error messages.

## 6. Check the battery
If it's been a few years, the battery is a likely culprit. Signs of a failing battery:
• Short run times
• Shows charged but dies quickly
• Charging errors, or it won't hold a charge consistently

To check the connection:
• Remove the bottom cover (a few screws), take the battery out, check the connector for dirt or corrosion, and reseat it firmly.
• A replacement e-series battery is fairly inexpensive. iRobot-brand is safest, though reputable third-party ones work.

## 7. Error codes
If the robot announces a "Charging Error" with a number, tell me the number and I can narrow it down. For example, Charging Error 1 usually means the battery isn't connected properly, and Error 5 often relates to temperature or the battery itself.

If none of this works, contact iRobot support, especially if it's still under warranty.

How old is your e5, and does it show any lights or error messages when it fails to charge?
its about 4 years old. app says Charging error 5 and the ring goes red with a two-tone sound. no burning smell or anything

Charging Error 5 points to a fault in the charging system, and on a 4-year-old e5 that combined with intermittent charging most often means the battery is wearing out. Before buying a new one, try these quick steps, since they sometimes clear it.

## 1. Reboot the robot
• Hold the CLEAN button for about 20 seconds until the light ring swirls white, then release.
• Put it back on the dock and see if the error returns.

## 2. Reseat the battery
A loose or dirty battery connection can trigger this error.
1. Flip the robot over and remove the two screws on the battery door (Phillips screwdriver).
2. Lift the battery out using its pull tab.
3. Check the battery and robot connectors for dust, corrosion, or bent pins. Clean gently with a dry cloth or a bit of rubbing alcohol.
4. Reinsert it firmly, replace the cover, and try charging again.

## 3. Rule out temperature and power issues
• Keep the robot and dock in a normal room temperature spot, away from heaters, direct sunlight, or cold garages.
• Make sure the contacts on the robot and dock are clean (from the earlier steps).

## 4. If the error keeps coming back: replace the battery
At 4 years old, this is the likely fix and a fairly cheap one.
• You need the iRobot Lithium-Ion battery for the e & i series (the same battery fits both).
• Buy from iRobot or a reputable seller. Very cheap no-name batteries can cause repeat errors or be unsafe.
• Swapping it uses the same steps as reseating above.

## 5. If a new battery doesn't fix it
The problem is likely the robot's charging circuit or the dock. At that point:
• If you can borrow or buy a spare dock, test it to rule out the Home Base.
• Contact iRobot Support. The warranty has probably expired, but they can confirm the diagnosis and may offer repair or upgrade options.

Good sign: no burning smell or swelling means nothing unsafe is going on. If you ever notice the battery swelling, getting hot, or leaking, stop using it and dispose of it at a battery recycling point.
i wiped the contacts on the dock and the robot with alcohol earlier, and it's charged every night for 4 days now with no error. haven't tried the battery reseat though. is that still needed?

No, you can skip it for now. If it's charged reliably for 4 nights straight, dirty contacts were almost certainly the cause, and the battery reseat was really a "next step if the error persists" fix. Opening it up when it's working doesn't gain you much.

Going forward:
• Clean the contacts every few weeks (more often if you have pets or lots of carpet). That's your main prevention.
• Watch for the error coming back. If Charging Error 5 returns even with clean contacts, then try the reseat, and if that doesn't help, replace the battery.
• Keep an eye on run time. At 4 years old the battery is still aging. If cleaning sessions get noticeably shorter or it dies before finishing, a new battery is worth it regardless of errors.

Glad the simple fix did it.
